items.claim: A setumah stands after MT 20:1, inside this row's span of MT 20:1-26, and the row leaves it undisclosed. It discloses the petuchah after MT 19:14, the setumah after MT 20:26 and the count-only disjunctive stroke at MT 20:1, but not the paragraph mark carried by that same verse. The messenger formula at MT 20:3 and at MT 20:5 likewise sits inside the span undisclosed by role, although the MT 20:3 splice carries it in its own quoted bytes.
items.both_sides: Onset side: the petuchah after MT 19:14 opens the paragraph at MT 20:1, and MT 20:1 carries the year-month-day dateline while the strict word-event onset follows at MT 20:2 - under the ruled reading a dateline that carries no word-event opens a narrative frame, and the word-event after it is a sub-onset inside that frame. Close side: the setumah after MT 20:26 is met by a fresh messenger formula with the son-of-man address at MT 20:27. Both outer edges hold on the bytes. The interior setumah after MT 20:1 divides the dateline verse from the word-event verse, so it corroborates the frame-plus-sub-onset reading the row already argues rather than calling for a cut: a cut there would leave MT 20:1 as a one-verse unit and strand the oracle's own onset in the next unit.

suggested_fix.fact: the setumah after MT 20:1 lies inside the span and corroborates reading MT 20:1 as the dateline frame with the word-event at MT 20:2 as its sub-onset; the messenger formula stands at MT 20:3 and at MT 20:5, also inside the span

items.claim: The onset at MT 20:27 is true on the bytes: that verse carries both the son-of-man address and the messenger formula, and it stands immediately after the setumah that closes MT 20:26. MT 20:27-29 carries no paragraph mark, no disjunctive stroke, no ketiv/qere note and no editorial note, and the row's statement that its end is triggered by the next onset rather than by a refrain is accurate - MT 20:29 carries no close formula, and a fresh messenger formula stands at MT 20:30.
items.both_sides: Onset side: the setumah after MT 20:26 together with the son-of-man address and messenger formula at MT 20:27. Close side: MT 20:29 ends on the high-place etymology with neither a close formula nor a mark, so the row's end rests on the messenger-formula onset at MT 20:30. The row states that asymmetry as weaker close-side evidence instead of claiming a refrain it does not have, which is the honest reading of the bytes.

items.claim: Every Hebrew fact holds. The messenger formula opens MT 20:30; the as-I-live oath stands at MT 20:31 and again at MT 20:33, each with the utterance signature; no paragraph mark falls anywhere inside MT 20:30-38; and the count discipline at the close is exact - the you-shall-know refrain closing MT 20:38 is a second-person-plural form belonging to the 21-verse plural set, not to the 28-verse third-person-plural set, which carries no verse of MT chapter 20 or MT chapter 21 at all. I re-derived both sets from the consonantal text and they reproduce at 21 and at 28.
items.both_sides: Onset side: the messenger formula at MT 20:30, standing behind the etymological aside that ends at MT 20:29 with no close formula. Close side: the plural you-shall-know refrain at MT 20:38, immediately before the address turn and fresh messenger formula at MT 20:39. Both sides are formula-marked and the tradition places no paragraph mark inside the stretch, so the nine-verse unit holds without an interior seam.

items.claim: The close is byte-true and doubly marked: MT 20:44 carries both the utterance signature and the second-person-plural you-shall-know refrain and is followed by a petuchah, and it is the third and last of exactly three plural recognition verses in MT chapter 20 - MT 20:38, MT 20:42 and MT 20:44 - a set I re-derived from the consonantal text. The interior refrain at MT 20:42 is disclosed rather than used as a seam. The onset at MT 20:39 carries the address turn to the house of Israel together with the messenger formula, and the row refuses to let either witness's chapter numbering do boundary work.
items.both_sides: Close side: the utterance signature and the plural recognition refrain at MT 20:44, with a petuchah after that verse. Onset side of what follows: the strict word-event onset at MT 21:1 = WEB 20:45. Both sides carry a formula, and the tradition's paragraph mark sits exactly at the seam, so the high grade is earned from the text rather than from the chapter break that happens to coincide with it - which is what the row itself says.

items.claim: Three devices lie inside this row's span, WEB 20:45-49 = MT 21:1-5, undisclosed by role: the son-of-man address and the direction opener at MT 21:2 = WEB 20:46, and the messenger formula together with the behold-I-am form at MT 21:3 = WEB 20:47. The direction opener is the standard onset corroboration for a word-event unit, and across this book it is disclosed at seven of the nine spans that carry it. The boundary itself, the mark claims, the mashal-root claim and the single-witness note claim are all true on the bytes.
items.both_sides: Onset side: the strict word-event onset at MT 21:1 = WEB 20:45, with the petuchah after MT 20:44 standing behind it. Close side: the doubled mashal root at MT 21:5 = WEB 20:49, with a petuchah after that verse. Both sides carry a formula and a paragraph mark, so the span is right, and the undisclosed devices are onset corroboration and an interior speech opener that change nothing about where the edges fall. Disclosing them strengthens the row: the same chain recurs verse for verse in the unit that follows, and that parallel is what shows the two are twin units rather than one.

items.claim: Four facts inside this row's span, WEB 21:1-5 = MT 21:6-10, are undisclosed: the son-of-man address and the direction opener at MT 21:7 = WEB 21:2; the messenger formula at MT 21:8 = WEB 21:3, which stands in the short form without the divine-title pair and is one of only three such verses in the book; the behold-I-am-against-you form in that same verse; and the single-witness editorial note carried by every one of MT 21:6 to MT 21:10. The boundary, the two mark claims, the recognition-family classification and the byte-identity claim about the two onsets are all true.
items.both_sides: Onset side: the strict word-event onset at MT 21:6 = WEB 21:1, byte-equal codepoint for codepoint to the onset at MT 21:1 = WEB 20:45, with the petuchah after MT 21:5 = WEB 20:49 standing behind it. Close side: MT 21:10 = WEB 21:5 carries the all-flesh they-shall-know refrain, a member of the 64-verse wider family and not of the 28-verse strict set, and a setumah follows that verse. Both sides are marked, so the span holds. The continuity argument on the other side is real and the row discloses it rather than hiding it: the same all-flesh subject stands at MT 21:4 = WEB 20:48, there with the seeing verb instead of the knowing verb, and a repeated onset formula introducing a restatement of the unit just closed is the shape that makes a merged reading arguable - which is why medium is better calibrated here than high would be.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Inside MT 20:1-26 the two sabbath notices are described together as gifts, but on the bytes MT 20:12 states the giving while MT 20:20 is a command to hallow what was given.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: a descriptor that reads like a byte claim invites a later pass to re-derive it and open a finding over wording rather than over data; the distinction touches no boundary.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether a row whose span carries the single-witness editorial-note layer must disclose it. Across this book, 27 of the 37 spans that carry the layer mention it and 10 do not, and the two twin units in the numbering zone split, the earlier disclosing it and the later not.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: if disclosure is required, the omission reaches more spans than this cluster; if it is optional, my note-layer point belongs on the record as a convention question and not as a row defect.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The 21-verse second-person-plural you-shall-know set that two of these rows rely on is carried by the ruled book strategy and not by the frame inventory, whose own second-person entry is a different, five-verse singular set.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: a later lane re-deriving the close-family counts from the frame inventory alone would get five and not 21, and could reopen a correct row; I re-derived 21 from the consonantal text and it reproduces exactly.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: No ketiv/qere site falls anywhere in MT 20:1-21:10, so the already-routed question about read forms rendered without the source's morpheme separator, or read forms occurring only in the apparatus, has zero instances in my cluster.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: the open question needs instance data, and the honest contribution from this cluster is a nil return, which is not evidence either way.

e19_selfreport: I ran no listing, no glob, no wildcard and no recursive search anywhere, including my own scratch. Every file I opened was opened by the exact path named in my brief, my launch message, or the ledger my brief names for the write-authority check. My private working files went into a uniquely named subdirectory of my own session scratchpad, created without testing for it, and I wrote nothing under the worktree and no receipt.
